title: Career growth scratch catalogue
content:
Purpose / quick note:
This is a messy scratchpad for my upcoming 1:1 with Priya (manager) and for the mid-year calibration. I want a single place with concrete signals, anecdotes, and clear asks so we don't wander in the meeting.

Top goals (6-12 months) — concrete and measurable:
- Ownership: Lead the ops onboarding revamp project and reduce time-to-productive for new hires from 14 days -> 7 days (metric: average days until first independent ticket handled).
- Team health: Establish a regular new-hire buddy program, target NPS >= 8 for first-30-days feedback (survey to be created).
- Systems: Migrate manual, spreadsheet-based headcount tracker to a lightweight internal tool or Notion template with automated updates from payroll by end of Q3.
- Influence: Run 2 cross-functional postmortems (engineering + product) for hiring/process incidents and deliver 3 improvement experiments with measurable outcomes.
- Career dev: Present at internal all-hands on ops best practices (30-min) and publish 1 playbook in Confluence.

Recent wins (last 3 months) — quick bullets I can say out loud:
- Reduced time-to-offer by ~10% by streamlining final interview coordination (took ownership of scheduler templates and interviewer prep).
- Piloted a simplified job offer pack that decreased candidate email back-and-forth (anecdote: hiring manager DM'd saying it felt "so much cleaner").
- Coordinated a cross-team hiring forecast for product which avoided an over-commitment of contractors for Feb.

Evidence / stories to bring up (specifics matter):
- Example 1: Feb 3 scheduling overhaul — I scripted a new interviewer prep checklist, saving ~30 minutes per committee. Linked doc: HR-4387 (Jira).
- Example 2: Candidate experience tweak — created the "offer explainer" doc; feedback from candidate (R. Patel) noted "clear and transparent" in an email. I saved that thread in Slack.
- Example 3: Incident postmortem — worked with SRE to run blameless postmortem on corrupted offer spreadsheet; I coordinated fixes and owner assignments; outcome: new S3 backup + converted spreadsheet to read-only.

Areas of improvement — honest notes I should voice and own:
- Delegation: I still get pulled into scheduling minutiae; need to train one contractor to take over recurring tasks by June.
- Quantification: I need better dashboards; many of my asks are qualitative — create a weekly ops dashboard (thin) by April to show progress.
- Upward influence: practice short "ask" scripts for execs — rehearsal goal: 3x before next skip-level.

Ask for manager (Priya) — clear, prioritized asks:
1) Career calibration: I would like prioritization on a promotion readiness conversation and clarity on the remaining bar to reach L5. Request: a short calibration note and 2 concrete examples of where my work needs to expand.
2) Bandwidth: Approval to hire a 0.5 FTE contract for scheduling & onboarding ops for Q2 (budget already discussed with finance informally).
3) Visibility: Sponsor me to run the May all-hands ops slot (30 min).
4) Mentorship: One skip-level intro to the Head of Talent for 20 minutes to discuss strategic ops exposure.

Open questions / follow-ups (for meeting):
- Do we have a formal rubric for L4->L5 in people-ops? If yes, where is it stored? If not, can we draft one? (linked artifact Confluence request).
- Will finance sign off on 0.5 FTE contractor before my ask goes to People Ops leadership? Who is the approver?
- Any upcoming headcount that would change priorities for the migration project?

Quick metrics I want in the next 2 weeks (data asks):
- Average days to first independent ticket (by cohort).
- New-hire first-30-day NPS score (sample size >= 8).
- Number of manual spreadsheets in use across ops (rough inventory).

Tiny experiment ideas (low cost) to mention:
- "Offer explainer" A/B test: add a one-page FAQ to the offer email for 50% of candidates and measure reply rate/time to accept.
- Buddy check-in automation: short automated Slack check-in at day 7 and 21, measure NPS later.

Prep checklist for the 1:1 (things to bring):
- 3 quick slides (one-pager) showing goals, asks, and recent wins.
- Linked threads/emails that support the anecdotes (search terms: "offer explainer", "scheduling overhaul").
- Draft contractor JD for 0.5 FTE.

Notes-to-self (meta & tone):
- Keep it factual and short: manager has limited time — lead with the promotion ask, then bandwidth.
- Use data and one anecdote. Don't apologize for being assertive.
- End with a specific next step and timeline.

Misc scratch items (random scribbles):
- Consider running a "new hire shadow day" where ops shadows the first day of 2 new hires to capture friction (1/4 effort).
- Follow up on Confluence playbook: assign a 2-week deadline to publish a draft.

Version notes:
- v0.1: initial messy scratchpad created 2026-02-28.
- v0.2: added contractor JD outline 2026-03-03.
- v0.3: trimmed and prioritized asks 2026-03-10.

End of document.
